frontier.hypothesis: The dependence-delay lever proven by d1 works but overshoots by six slots and pays a load (+2 insns). A delay of exactly one cycle, sourced from an insn already present in the window, would land the base insn on the target's slot 91 at 176 instructions.
frontier.mechanism: sched.c:1497 makes only a load's consumer cost 2; every other producer in the window costs 1. The overshoot in d1 comes from the 2-cycle load plus the extra lw occupying a ready slot. A 1-cycle producer would delay the base insn by exactly one issue slot - which is the whole distance between slot 88 and the position the target wants - without changing the instruction count.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate every insn already emitted in the contested window (the shift chain's srl, the xor, the gp store, the s.zero18 store, the previous half's spilled 0x40(sp) reload) and find a spelling in which the a2 base legally reads one of them. Concretely: route r4 through the SAME expression tree that produces the third rnd's operand (e.g. spell the base as an expression whose operand is the xor result masked to zero-contribution is NOT allowed - it must be a real value), or exploit the half-2-only 0x40(sp) reload the target already performs and check whether half 2 alone rotates. Measure with tools/sweep_variants.py and require build_insns == 176 before crediting anything.

frontier.hypothesis: Half 1 and half 2 may not need the same lever: the target already spills base_offset to 0x40(sp) and reloads it in half 2 only, so half 2 already contains a load in its window while half 1 does not.
frontier.mechanism: The residual is 3 slots per half. If a form exists that fixes only half 2 (whose window already has 'lw a3,0x40(sp)' available as a 2-cycle producer), the floor drops from 6 to 3 without touching half 1 - and a 3-floor is a strictly better platform for the next lever than the current symmetric 6.
frontier.next_probe: Sweep asymmetric forms: apply the d1 array spelling to half 2's base only (keeping half 1's scalar), and separately try making half 2's base read from the same 0x40(sp) slot the target already reloads. Score each and record whether the half-2 rotation flips independently of half 1's - no session has yet measured the two halves as separable.

frontier.hypothesis: Frontier item 1 from s7 (an a2 base insn MANUFACTURED by combine at a late i3 position) is still untested; s8 tested only source-level reassociations, all of which cse/combine re-canonicalise back to the same pair.
frontier.mechanism: combine.c places a combined insn at i3's position, so the LUID a sched1 tie-break reads is i3's, not the source statement's. The s8 sweep (v4) shows source association cannot reach this; the insn must be one combine CREATES, which requires a source form where the base does not exist as an insn until combine splits or merges something later in the block.
frontier.next_probe: Diff tmp/grind/func_8005D554/s7/dumps2/text1b.rtl against .combine over the block-6 region to enumerate which insns combine creates and where it places them (this diff has still never been read), then sweep source forms whose a2 base is only materialised by that pass. Confirm build_insns stays 176 before crediting.
